He played [[college basketball]] for the [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU Tigers]]. Reid won the [[NBA Sixth Man of the Year Award]] in 2024.{{Cite web |title=Naz Reid Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft Status and more |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/r/reidna01.html |access-date=2024-08-09 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}} He recently signed a three-year $42 million contract with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], before being traded to the Hornets in the summer of 2026.{{Cite web |title=Minnesota Timberwolves, center Naz Reid agree to $42M deal - UPI.com |url=https://www.upi.com/Sports_News/NBA/2023/06/26/Minnesota-Timberwolves-Naz-Reid-42M-deal/2611687779515/ |access-date=2026-02-16 |website=UPI |language=en}} ==High school career== Reid grew up in [[Asbury Park, New Jersey]] with his mother, Anashia, and sisters Toraya and Jakahya.{{Cite web |last=Marsh |first=Steve |date=2023-12-18 |title=In Conversation with Naz Reid |url=https://mspmag.com/arts-and-culture/in-conversation-with-naz-reid/ |access-date=2025-02-13 |website=Mpls.St.Paul Magazine |language=en-us}} He attended [[Roselle Catholic High School]].Edelson, Stephen. [https://www.app.com/story/sports/high-school/2015/06/02/roselle-catholic-us-basketball-nazreon-reid/28342227/ "Asbury Park's Nazreon Reid makes the most of his experiences"], ''[[Asbury Park Press]]'', June 2, 2015. Accessed July 18, 2018. "It's been a heck of a ride over the past year for Nazreon Reid, the 6-10 Asbury Park native who has had intriguing college coaches since he was in middle school.... When high school began, Reid started making the daily trek up to Roselle Catholic, where the freshman would play for the state's latest powerhouse program." Following his senior season, in which he averaged 14.8 points, 7.7 rebounds, and 2.1 blocks per game, Reid was invited to the [[2018 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]]. During the game, he scored 15 points, had 11 rebounds, two assists, and one block while playing for 20 minutes.{{cite news|title=2018 McDonald's All-American Game: Nazreon Reid represents New Jersey well|author=Christie, Sherlon|url=https://www.app.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2018/03/28/2018-mcdonalds-all-american-game-nazreon-reid-represents-new-jersey-well/468028002/|date=March 28, 2018|accessdate=July 1, 2018|work=[[Asbury Park Press]]}} Reid scored 22 points as Roselle Catholic defeated Don Bosco Prep in the NJSIAA Tournament of Champions.{{cite news |last1=Edelson |first1=Stephen |title=Boys Hoops: Asbury Park's Naz Reid goes out on top, as Roselle Catholic wins TOC |url=https://www.app.com/story/sports/high-school/2018/03/18/boys-hoops-naz-reid-goes-out-top-roselle-catholic-wins-toc/431863002/ |accessdate=July 17, 2018 |work=[[Asbury Park Press]] |date=March 18, 2018}} During his high school career he was a member of the Jelly Fam, an internet movement focused around wild finger roll layups. Nicknamed "Big Jelly", he was known for playing like a big and flashy guard.{{Cite web |last=Klopfer |first=Brady |date=2022-12-16 |title=NBA nicknames deserved their own Hall of Fame so we made one |url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2022/12/16/23512368/nba-basketball-reference-nicknames-evan-fournier-kyrie-irving |access-date=2023-02-28 |website=SBNation.com |language=en}} He was the only member of the movement to make it to the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]].{{Cite web |date=2021-11-13 |title=Minnesota Timberwolves Roundup: Naz Reid talks, Anthony Edwards meets Adam Sandler |url=https://dunkingwithwolves.com/2021/11/13/minnesota-timberwolves-roundup-naz-reid-talks-anthony-edwards-meets-adam-sandler/ |access-date=2023-02-28 |website=Dunking with Wolves |language=en-US}} In January 2025, his high school retired his number - 5 - in a ceremony he and his Timberwolves teammates attended in the school gym in [[Roselle, New Jersey]].{{Cite web |date=2025-01-17 |title=NBA Sixth Man of The Year Has His High School Jersey Number Retired |url=https://www.si.com/high-school/new-jersey/nba-sixth-man-of-the-year-has-his-high-school-jersey-number-retired-01jhtf7pqfyc |access-date=2025-05-21 |website=High School On SI |language=en-US}} ===Recruiting=== Reid was a consensus 5-star recruit in high school, ranked the best power forward in New Jersey and the third-best power forward in the U.S., as well as the 22nd-best player in his class by 247 sports. On September 12, 2017, Reid committed to play college basketball at LSU (Louisiana State University), with his friend Matthew McMahon.{{cite web|title=4-Star PF Prospect Nazreon Reid Commits to LSU over Arizona|author=Wells, Adam|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2722628-4-star-pf-prospect-nazreon-reid-commits-to-lsu-over-arizona|date=September 12, 2017|accessdate=July 1, 2018|work=Bleacher Report}} Reid later said, "What drew me to the school is Coach Wade, [assistant] Coach [[Greg Heiar]], all the other coaches."{{cite web|title=LSU signee Nazreon Reid honored to showcase skill at McDonald's All-American Game|author=Whelan Jr., Tim|url=http://usatodayhss.com/2018/lsu-signee-nazreon-reid-receives-mcdonalds-all-american-game-jersey|date=January 31, 2018|accessdate=July 1, 2018|work=[[USA Today]]}} {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2018}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Naz Reid | position = [[Power forward (basketball)|PF]] | hometown = [[Asbury Park, New Jersey|Asbury Park, NJ]] | highschool = [[Roselle Catholic High School|Roselle Catholic]] (NJ) | feet = 6 | inches = 10 | weight = 240 | 40 = | commitdate = September 12, 2017 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 93 }} {{College athlete recruit end | 40 = | year = 2018 | rivals ref title = LSU 2018 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2018 LSU Tigers Recruiting Class | 247 ref title = | rivals school = lsu | 247 school = | espn schoolid = 99 | scout overall = | rivals overall = 21 | 247 overall = 22 | espn overall = 12 | accessdate = June 4, 2018 | bball = yes }} ==College career== Reid made his college debut on November 6, 2018, with 17 points and 6 rebounds in a 94–63 win over [[Southeastern Louisiana University]]. Three days later, he scored his season-high 29 points, along with 7 rebounds, and shooting 4–6 behind the arc. Throughout his freshman season, Reid averaged 13.6 points, 7.2 rebounds, and 0.9 assists. On April 3, 2019, he declared for the [[2019 NBA draft]] and hired an agent, foregoing his final three years of college eligibility.{{cite news |last1=Embody |first1=Billy |title=Naz Reid declares for 2019 NBA Draft |url=https://247sports.com/college/lsu/Article/Naz-Reid-LSU-basketball-2019-NBA-Draft-declares-130854194/ |accessdate=March 23, 2020 |work=247 Sports |date=April 3, 2019}} == Professional career == === Minnesota Timberwolves (2019–2026) === After going undrafted in the 2019 NBA draft, Reid signed with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) on July 5, 2019, on a [[two-way contract]] with the Timberwolves' [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Iowa Wolves]]. Under that deal's terms, Reid would split time between Minnesota and Iowa.{{cite web |title=TIMBERWOLVES SIGN NAZ REID TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-sign-naz-reid-two-way-contract |publisher=NBA |accessdate=July 7, 2019 |language=en |date=July 5, 2019}} He also played for Minnesota in the [[2019 NBA Summer League]]. On July 17, Reid signed a multi-year contract with the Timberwolves.{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-sign-naz-reid-multi-year-contract|title=Timberwolves Sign Naz Reid to Multi-Year Contract|work=NBA.com|accessdate=July 18, 2019|date=July 17, 2019}} He was assigned to the Timberwolves' [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Iowa Wolves]], for opening night of the G League season.{{cite news |last1=Lawhon |first1=Danny |title=New energy and a familiar face bring Iowa Wolves into 2019-20 NBA G League season |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/basketball/iowa-wolves/2019/11/07/iowa-wolves-nba-g-league-lindell-wigginton-keita-bates-diop-minnesota-timberwolves/2519525001/ |accessdate=November 26, 2019 |work=[[Des Moines Register]] |date=November 7, 2019}} Reid made his NBA debut on December 8, scoring three points in a 125–142 loss to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{Cite web |title=DAVIS SCORES 50, POWERS LAKERS TO 142-125 WIN OVER T-WOLVES |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021900342 |access-date=February 3, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On January 13, 2020, he scored a season-high 20 points in a 104–117 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{Cite web |title=GILGEOUS-ALEXANDER'S FIRST TRIPLE-DOUBLE LEADS THUNDER |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021900594 |access-date=February 3, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On February 6, 2021, Reid scored a career-high 29 points, alongside six rebounds and two steals, in a 118–120 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{Cite web |title=THUNDER SCORE 83 IN HALF, THEN RALLY TO EDGE WOLVES 120-118 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000359 |access-date=February 3, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On January 2, 2022, Reid scored a season-high 23 points, alongside 11 rebounds, in a 103–108 loss to the Lakers.{{Cite web |title=JAMES, MONK HELP LAKERS EDGE TIMBERWOLVES 108-103 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100551 |access-date=February 3, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} He was a key reserve on a Timberwolves team that qualified for their first postseason appearance since [[2018 NBA playoffs|2018]]. Reid made his first playoff appearance during the first round of the playoffs on April 16, recording two rebounds in a 130–117 Game 1 win over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{Cite web |title=TIMBERWOLVES STUN GRIZZLIES, GRAB GAME 1 WITH 130-117 WIN |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042100151 |access-date=February 3, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} The Timberwolves lost to the Grizzlies in six games. On December 16, 2022, during his first start of the season, Reid scored a season-high 28 points and grabbed nine rebounds to help Minnesota to a 112–110 win over the Thunder.[https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/national/story/2022-12-16/reid-scores-28-as-timberwolves-top-thunder-snap-3-game-skid Reid scores 28 as Timberwolves top Thunder, snap 3-game skid] On February 1, 2023, he recorded 24 points, 13 rebounds and four assists in a 119–114 overtime win over the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{Cite web |title=RUSSELL, EDWARDS HELP TIMBERWOLVES BEAT WARRIORS IN OT |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200774 |access-date=February 3, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On March 29, during a 107–100 loss to the [[Phoenix Suns]], Reid suffered a left wrist injury in the fourth quarter. Two days later, the Timberwolves announced that he was diagnosed with a left [[scaphoid fracture]] of his left wrist and would be out indefinitely.{{Cite web |title=Naz Reid Injury Update |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/naz-reid-injury-update |access-date=March 31, 2023 |website=NBA}} On June 25, 2023, Reid signed a three-year $42 million contract extension with the Timberwolves. The extension included a player option for the 2025–26 season.{{Cite web |title=Timberwolves, center Naz Reid agree on 3-year, $42M deal|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/37914752/timberwolves-center-naz-reid-agree-3-year-42m-deal}} On March 8, 2024, Reid scored a career-high 34 points during a 113–104 loss against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].[https://www.si.com/nba/timberwolves/news/cavs-outlast-wolves-in-overtime-despite-naz-reids-34-points Cavs outlast Wolves in overtime despite Naz Reid's 34 points] On April 24, 2024, he received the [[NBA Sixth Man of the Year Award]].{{Cite web |title=Wolves' Naz Reid named 2023-24 Kia NBA Sixth Man of the Year |url=https://www.nba.com/news/kia-nba-sixth-man-2023-24-naz-reid |access-date=April 25, 2024 |website=NBA.com}} Reid made 80 appearances (17 starts) for Minnesota during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 14.2 points, 6.0 rebounds, and 2.3 assists. On June 27, 2025, Reid and the Timberwolves agreed to a five-year, $125 million contract extension.{{cite web | last=Fonseca | first=Bryan | title=Naz Reid lands massive $125 million Timberwolves extension | website=New York Post | date=2025-06-28 | url=https://nypost.com/2025/06/27/sports/naz-reid-lands-massive-125m-timberwolves-contract-extension/ | access-date=2025-12-07}} On February 9, 2026, Reid was ejected from a game against the [[2025–26 Atlanta Hawks season|Atlanta Hawks]] after being involved in an altercation with [[Mouhamed Gueye]] early in the fourth quarter.{{Cite web|title=Naz Reid, Mouhamed Gueye tossed after altercation late in game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/47883208/naz-reid-mouhamed-gueye-tossed-altercation-late-game|access-date=March 31, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} He and Gueye were both subsequently fined $35,000 for the incident.{{Cite web|title=Hawks’ Mouhamed Gueye, Wolves’ Naz Reid fined $35K for altercation|url=https://www.nba.com/news/mouhamed-gueye-naz-reid-fined-altercation|access-date=March 31, 2026|website=nba.com|language=en}} In March 2026, Reid was fined $50,000 for questioning the integrity of the officials by the NBA. He was thrown out by referee Scott Foster during the game against [[Houston Rockets]].{{cite web |title=Naz Reid fined for questioning 'integrity' of NBA officials |url=https://basketnews.com/news-243939-naz-reid-fined-for-questioning-integrity-of-nba-officials.html#google_vignette |website=basketnews.com |access-date=15 April 2026 |language=en}} === Charlotte Hornets (2026–present) === On July 10, 2026, Reid, alongside the draft rights to [[Matteo Spagnolo]], a 2033 first-round pick, three second-round picks, and three first-round pick swaps, was traded to the [[Charlotte Hornets]] as part of a four-team trade.{{Cite web |title=Charlotte Hornets Acquire Naz Reid, Multiple Draft Picks From Minnesota For Lamelo Ball And Josh Green |url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/charlotte-hornets-acquire-naz-reid-multiple-draft-picks-from-minnesota-for-lamelo-ball-and-josh-green |access-date=July 10, 2026 |publisher=[[Charlotte Hornets]]}} == Fan reception == Despite serving as the [[Minnesota Timberwolves|Minnesota Timberwolves’]] backup center, Naz Reid has developed a strong following among fans in [[Minnesota]].{{Cite web |date=2024-08-07 |title=The Legend of Naz Reid: The Reigning Sixth Man of the Year Covers SLAM 251 |url=https://www.slamonline.com/the-magazine/251/naz-reid-slam-cover-story-251/ |access-date=2025-02-25 |website=SLAM |language=en}} The ''Minnesota Star Tribune'' has noted that his name has become widely used among Timberwolves supporters, describing it as a form of shared expression within the fan community.{{Cite web |last=Scoggins |first=Chip |date=2023-11-05 |title=Why there's a Naz Reid cult following among Timberwolves fans |url=https://www.startribune.com/timberwolves-naz-reid-cult-following-chip-scoggins/600317108 |access-date=2025-02-25 |website=www.startribune.com |language=en}} At a March 22, 2024 game, the Timberwolves gave away beach towels emblazoned with his name—they would later sell for more than $100 on [[eBay]].{{Cite news |last=Krawczynski |first=Jon |title=Driven by the loss of his mentor, Naz Reid made the fight against cancer personal |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5712476/2024/08/22/naz-reid-cayden-addison-blood-stem-cell-donor/ |access-date=2025-02-25 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}} During their 2024 playoff series against the [[Denver Nuggets]], a tattoo artist in [[Roseville, Minnesota|Roseville]] offered $20 tattoos of his name. Over 200 people took him up on it.{{Cite web |date=2024-05-16 |title='It's crazy': Timberwolves fans go viral for Naz Reid tattoos during playoff run |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/40155587/naz-reid-minnesota-timberwolves-2024-nba-playoffs-tattoos |access-date=2025-02-25 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} Later that month, a local pizzeria went viral for their “Honk if you love Naz Reid” sign. A contestant on [[Jeopardy!]] even revealed she had named her cat after him (stylized as NAZ REID).{{Cite web |title=Naz Reid becomes a Timberwolves breakout star |url=https://www2.startribune.com/naz-reid-sixth-man-of-year-minnesota-timberwolves/600358955/ |access-date=2025-02-25 |website=Star Tribune}} At the 2024 [[Minnesota State Fair]], [https://www.cropart.com/cagall01.htm crop artists] including [https://www.cropart.com/TaraC.dir/2024_tc_NazSeed.htm Tara Cantwell], [https://www.cropart.com/sjerome.dir/2024_sj_NazReid.htm Sarah
